subject: measurement error + hierarchical model from WinBUGS to stan

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: measurement error + hierarchical model from WinBUGS to stan
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to move the simple measurement error + hierarchical model to stan and encounter severe difficulties including divergence and low estimated Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information. The WinBUGS model is extremely simple: we have bunch of lots each of which have measurements (assay) of individual tablets. The model below estimates measurement error (analytical variability sigmaA), inter-lot variability sigmaB, intra-lot variability sigmaW, and processMean without any problems. But when I am trying to run the seemingly equivalent stan code the estimates for process mean and inter-lot variability are similar between bugs and stan while stan estimates of sigmaW and sigmaA are completely strange, pairs plot shows very funny shapes and trace plot shows strong autocorrelations for sigmaA and sigmaW. I guess it is some sort of nonidentiafiability of sigmaA and sigmaW and wonder if there are ways to separate the two.

Thanks for any suggestions,
Linas

stan model:
model {
    sigmaA ~ normal (0, 2);
    processMean ~ normal (100, 10);
    sigmaW ~ normal (0, 2);
    sigmaB ~ normal (0, 2);
    mu ~ normal (processMean, sigmaB);
    for (n in 1 : N) {
        Y_true [n] ~ normal (mu [lot [n]], sigmaW);
    }
    Y ~ normal (Y_true, sigmaA);
}

bugs model:
    model <- function ()
    {
        for (i in 1 : N) {
            Y_true [i] ~ dnorm (mu [lot [i]], tauW)
            Y [i] ~ dnorm (Y_true [i], tauA)
        }
        for (j in 1 : NLOTS) {
            mu [j] ~ dnorm (processMean, tauB)
        }
        tauW ~ dgamma (IG_alpha, IG_beta)
        sigmaW <- 1 / sqrt (tauW)
        processMean ~ dnorm (meanProcessMean, tauProcessMean)
        tauB ~ dgamma (IG_alpha, IG_beta)
        sigmaB <- 1 / sqrt (tauB)
        beta <- dfsigmaA / 2
        alpha <- beta * meansigmaA
        tauA ~ dgamma (alpha, beta)
        sigmaA <- 1 / sqrt (tauA)
    }

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] measurement error + hierarchical model from WinBUGS to stan
parts:
Sorry, you are right.

Linas

The full model is:

data {
int <lower=1> N; // number of samples
vector <lower=0> [N] Y; // weight of sample
int <lower=1> NLOTS; // number of lots
int <lower=1, upper=NLOTS> lot [N]; // lot# of sample
}
parameters {
vector [NLOTS] iii;
real processMean;
real <lower=0> sigmaB;
real <lower=0> sigmaW;
real <lower=0> sigmaA;
vector <lower=0> [N] Y_true;
}
model {
sigmaA ~ normal(0, 2);
processMean ~ normal(100, 10);
sigmaW ~ normal(0, 2);
sigmaB ~ normal(0, 2);
iii ~ normal(0, 1);
for (n in 1 : N)

Y_true[n] ~ normal(processMean + sigmaB * iii[lot[n]], sigmaW);
Y ~ normal(Y_true, sigmaA);
}

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Re[2]: [stan-users] measurement error + hierarchical model from WinBUGS to stan
parts:
After some reparametrization stan began to behave but now processMean
and sigmaW (intralot sd) differ significantly from bugs estimates while
sigmaB (inter lot sd) and sigmaA (analytical sd) are close.

Linas

data {
int <lower = 1> N;
vector <lower = 0> [N] Y; // weight of sample
int <lower = 1> NLOTS;

int <lower = 1, upper = NLOTS> lot [N]; // lot# of sample
real <lower = 0> meansigmaA;
real <lower = 0> dfsigmaA;
real <lower = 0> df;
real <lower = 0> scale;
}
transformed data {
real alpha;
real beta;

beta = dfsigmaA / 2;
alpha = beta * meansigmaA;

}
parameters {
vector [NLOTS] iii;
real processMean;
real <lower = 0> sigmaB;
real <lower = 0> sigmaW;
real <lower = 0> sigmaA;

vector <lower = 0> [N] Y_true_raw;
}
transformed parameters {
vector <lower = 0> [N] Y_true;
for (n in 1 : N)

Y_true [n] = processMean + sigmaB * iii [lot [n]] + Y_true_raw [n] *
sigmaW;
}
model {
sigmaA ~ inv_gamma (alpha, beta);
processMean ~ normal (100, 10);

sigmaW ~ student_t (df, 0, scale);
sigmaB ~ student_t (df, 0, scale);
iii ~ normal (0, 1);
Y_true_raw ~ normal (0, 1);

Y ~ normal (Y_true, sigmaA);
}


>

messages.author: a08a2def4527ebe2
messages.subject: Re: Re[2]: [stan-users] measurement error + hierarchical model from WinBUGS to stan
parts:
You use different priors in Bugs and Stan for sigmaW: 
Stan:
sigmaW ~ student_t (df, 0, scale);
Bugs:

tauW ~ dgamma (IG_alpha, IG_beta)
        sigmaW <- 1 / sqrt (tauW)
Could this be the cause of differing posteriors? What happens if you change the Stan model to exact same priors as in bugs?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] measurement error + hierarchical model from WinBUGS to stan
parts: I'm not surprised that sigmaW and SigmaA are correlated in this:

for (n in 1 : N) {
Y_true [n] ~ normal (mu [lot [n]], sigmaW);
}
Y ~ normal (Y_true, sigmaA);

I can suggest rewriting that to the following for efficiency and clarity:

Y_true ~ normal(mu[lot], sigmaW);
Y ~ normal(Y_true, sigmaA);

So Y is supposed to be a noisy measurement of Y_true?

You could try non-centering it:

Y_true_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
Y_true = mu[lot] + Y_true_raw * sigmaW;

- Bob

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] measurement error + hierarchical model from WinBUGS to stan
parts:
Thanks. After using a non-centered parametrization and strong prior for sigmaW the convergence became good. There are divergencies, but are much fewer. However, the estimate for sigmaW had blunt shape. sigmaW is intra lot variability and has skewed distribution so I thought I need to switch from normal sigmaW model to something skewed. So I tried johnson su (as in wikipedia)  and looks like was able to get estimates for sigmaA, sigmaB, and processMean the same as in bugs; mixing for other parameters was good. My question is why bugs gave very good estimates and then stan suddenly "indicated" that the model is not good enough. Does stan has some intrinsic capability to detect that model doesn't describe data well enough while bugs is less sensitive. I tried both WinBUGS and JAGS and they perfectly match each other.

Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] measurement error + hierarchical model from WinBUGS to stan
parts:
> On May 7, 2017, at 2:25 PM, Linas Mockus <linasm...@gmail.com> wrote:
>

> Thanks. After using a non-centered parametrization and strong prior for sigmaW the convergence became good. There are divergencies, but are much fewer. However, the estimate for sigmaW had blunt shape.
I don't know what that means.

> sigmaW is intra lot variability and has skewed distribution so I thought I need to switch from normal sigmaW model to something skewed. So I tried johnson su (as in wikipedia) and looks like was able to get estimates for sigmaA, sigmaB, and processMean the same as in bugs; mixing for other parameters was good. My question is why bugs gave very good estimates and then stan suddenly "indicated" that the model is not good enough.
How did Stan indicate that?
> Does stan has some intrinsic capability to detect that model doesn't describe data well enough while bugs is less sensitive. I tried both WinBUGS and JAGS and they perfectly match each other.

Yes. It explores the posterior better, so it can run off
into tails and narrow parts of the posterior that BUGS and JAGS
might not see. Did you run multiple chains from diffuse starting
points in both and estimate n_eff with Stan?

But as Andrew says, you should simulate from the model (not
from another model, but actually from the model you have, priors
and all), then see if BUGS and Stan recover the parameters.

- Bob
